public_rationale: Anthropic's April documentation reported average enterprise costs of about $13 per developer per active day, with 90% of users below $30 [e1]. Business Insider reported on April 29 that Anthropic linked the revised estimates to Opus 4.7 becoming Claude Code's primary model [e2]. These figures challenge the asserted minimum, but neither source identifies complete daily costs for particular recent models during April 1–28, 2026, so they do not settle the claim [e1, e2].
limitations: The aggregate figures do not disclose model shares, sampling dates or underlying daily usage records [e1, e2].
The spokesperson's explanation links the estimates to Opus 4.7 without identifying which models the users below $30 used [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Using Anthropic's recent models with Claude Code costs more than $30 per day.

statement.excerpt: These are astonishing numbers, made more so by the fact that there is no way you’re only spending $30 a day if you use any of Anthropic’s more-recent models.
statement.document_title: AI's Economics Don't Make Sense [Ad Free]

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that ordinary active development with recent Anthropic models necessarily exceeds $30 per developer per day.
The surrounding discussion makes this a claim about metered token costs, rather than subscription fees divided by calendar days.
Recent models means models available when the post appeared, including its explicit example, Opus 4.7.
I use April 2026 through the post date as the current observation period. The post specifies neither a measurement window nor a minimum daily workload.
criteria.support_condition: Model-specific daily usage evidence establishes a cost floor above $30 for ordinary active development with the recent models covered by the claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible usage records show ordinary active development with a recent model costing $30 or less per developer per active day, using the applicable token prices.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verified records from April 1–28, 2026 identifying recent models, ordinary development activity and complete daily token and cache charges. A qualifying active day costing $30 or less would contradict the claim; support would require model-specific evidence establishing the claimed daily cost floor.
